Chief_Complaint.content: Shortness of breath after insect sting

History_of_Present_Illness.content: Patient was stung on the arm a few minutes ago by an insect, possibly bee or wasp.

No medications taken yet for the reaction, including no antihistamines.
Patient denies previous history of anaphylaxis.

Past_Medical_History.content: History of occasional anxiety and panic attacks, never treated with medication.

Family_History.content: No known relevant family illnesses or acute reactions.

Assessment.content: Localized allergic reaction to insect sting (bee or wasp).
Assessment.source_text: 1) Localized allergic reaction to insect sting (bee/wasp).

Assessment.content: No visible lip swelling on examination.
History of occasional anxiety and panic.

Plan_of_Care.content: Recommend chlorphenamine (Piriton) 4 mg up to 6 times per day as an antihistamine option.
Alternative option is a once-daily over-the-counter antihistamine.
Patient advised to watch for lip swelling, shortness of breath, or stridor and to go straight to A&E if deterioration or rapid progression occurs.
Plan_of_Care.source_text: Safety-net: watch for lip swelling, SOB, stridor; if deterioration or rapid progression → go straight to A&E

Plan_of_Care.content: Monitor sting site and consider antibiotics if spreading redness, heat, or signs of local infection develop.
Plan_of_Care.source_text: Monitor sting site; if spreading redness/heat or signs of local infection → consider abx

Plan_of_Care.content: Education provided with a link on anaphylaxis.
Discussed that severe reactions usually occur immediately.
Plan_of_Care.source_text: discussed that severe reactions usually occur immediately

Plan_of_Care.content: No allergy testing indicated at present.
Consider blood tests if recurrent episodes or rashes occur.

Plan_of_Care.content: Advised low threshold to contact clinic for concerns.
